subject.title: fix(auth): bind OAuth and sessions to immutable identity

question: What supported recovery policy should existing email-owned sessions and durable records receive when migrating to immutable GitHub account IDs?
rationale: The branch intentionally changes the ownership contract for persisted records; choosing between migration, administrator-assisted recovery, and immediate invalidation is a security and upgrade-policy decision rather than a mechanical code correction.

options.title: Add verified one-time migration
options.body: Permit a legacy email-owned record to migrate only after a fresh authenticated GitHub login proves the same verified email under a defined expiry and audit boundary.

options.title: Use administrator-assisted recovery
options.body: Keep legacy identities denied by default but provide a documented administrator workflow to migrate durable ownership to a confirmed `github:<id>` value.

options.title: Accept immediate invalidation
options.body: Intentionally require recreation for every legacy session and durable record, with prominent upgrade documentation and operator communication.

recommendation.title: Add verified one-time migration
recommendation.body: Permit a legacy email-owned record to migrate only after a fresh authenticated GitHub login proves the same verified email under a defined expiry and audit boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: A current-main Worker authentication owner could not be established from the supplied review evidence, so the decision should be routed to the responsible auth-policy reviewer.
